[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Madrid]], Spain, which plays in [[La Liga]]. This chronological list comprises all those who have held the position of [[coach (sport)|manager]] of the first team of Real Madrid from 1910, when the first professional manager was appointed, to the present day. Each manager's entry includes his dates of tenure and the club's overall competitive record (in terms of matches won, drawn and lost), major honours won and significant achievements under his leadership. [[Caretaker manager]]s are included, where known. As of the end of the [[2024–25 Real Madrid CF season|2024–25]] season, Real Madrid have had 50 full-time managers.

The first full-time manager for Real Madrid was [[Arthur Johnson (footballer, born 1879)|Arthur Johnson]].<ref name="Arthur Johnson">{{cite web |title=Johnson |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041516841/1193040969580/contenido/Entrenador/Arthur_Jonhson.htm |publisher=Real Madrid CF |access-date=4 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120303021604/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041516841/1193040969580/contenido/Entrenador/Arthur_Jonhson.htm |archive-date=3 March 2012}}</ref> He was signed by one of the founders of Real Madrid, and then director, [[Adolfo Meléndez]], and coached the team for ten seasons, gaining one [[Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup]].

The most successful coach with Real Madrid is [[Carlo Ancelotti]], as he has won 15 titles with the team. Ancelotti, in two spells, won [[La Liga]] twice, [[Copa del Rey]] twice, [[UEFA Champions League]] three times, [[Supercopa de España|Spanish Super Cup]] twice, [[UEFA Super Cup]] three times, [[FIFA Club World Cup]] twice, and one [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]].

==Notes==
*<small>A</small>. {{note label|note01|A|^}} [[Campeonato Regional Centro|Campeonato Centro]] matches are not counted because it was a regional championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span-centrchamp.html|title=Spain – List of Champions of Centro|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=23 September 2009}}</ref>
*<small>B</small>. {{note label|note02|B|^}} Win % is [[Rounding|rounded]] to [[Decimal|two decimal places]].
*<small>C</small>. {{note label|player|C|a}}{{note label|player|C|b}}{{note label|player|C|c}}{{note label|player|C|d}}{{note label|player|C|e}}{{note label|player|C|f}}{{note label|player|C|g}}{{note label|player|C|h}}{{note label|player|C|i}}{{note label|player|C|j}}{{note label|player|C|k}}{{note label|player|C|l}}{{note label|player|C|m}}{{note label|player|C|n}}{{note label|player|C|o}}{{note label|player|C|p}}{{note label|player|C|q}}{{note label|player|C|r}}{{note label|player|C|s}}{{note label|player|C|t}}{{note label|player|C|u}}{{note label|player|C|v}} Formerly played for the club.
*<small>D</small>. {{note|Arthur}} [[Arthur Johnson (footballer, born 1879)|Arthur Johnson]] is the club's first full-time manager.
*<small>E</small>. {{note label|Llorente and Bernabéu|E|a}}{{note label|Llorente and Bernabéu|E|b}} [[Pedro Llorente]] and [[Santiago Bernabéu]] jointly managed the team from the dismissal of [[Juan de Cárcer]] until the appointment of [[José Ángel Berraondo]], so they share the same statistics.
*<small>F</small>. {{note|Villalonga}} [[José Villalonga]] is the first manager to manage a Spanish club side in European competition and to win a European trophy ([[1955–56 European Cup]]).
*<small>G</small>. {{note label|Muñoz|G|a}}{{note label|Muñoz|G|b}} [[Miguel Muñoz]] is the longest-serving manager in club history.
*<small>H</small>. {{note label|Remón and Luxemburgo|H|a}}{{note label|Remón and Luxemburgo|H|b}} [[Mariano García Remón]] and [[Vanderlei Luxemburgo]] share a victory against [[Real Sociedad]] in the [[La Liga]]. The match was suspended due to a [[bomb threat]] on 12 December 2004, with seven minutes remaining and the score at 1–1. It was resumed on 5 January 2005, and ended with a final score of 2–1.
*<small>I</small>. {{note label|Ancelotti|I|a}}{{note label|Ancelotti|I|b}} [[Carlo Ancelotti]] is the manager with most honours won in club history.
*<small>FIFA</small>. {{note label|fifa|FIFA|a}}{{note label|fifa|FIFA|b}}{{note label|fifa|FIFA|c}} Won [[FIFA World Coach of the Year]]/[[The Best FIFA Football Coach]] while at Real Madrid.
